chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave charity to a close relative. Is it correct for him to retract from it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but if he is in need, let him take from his close relative, from other than what he had given in charity to him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person take back a gift or charity given to a relative if they become poor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between revoking a gift and recovering its value, ruling that while the charity itself cannot be taken back, a needy giver may reclaim its worth from the recipient's general assets, excluding the specific donated item. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the gift (*hibah*) while accommodating the giver's financial needs, a principle often discussed in the context of *sadaqah* versus *hibah* in Shia fiqh. The distinction ensures that the recipient retains ownership of the specific object, preventing disputes over the exact item while allowing for equitable compensation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who gave charity with a charity to a friend. Is it correct for him that he retracts with regards to it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but if he is needy, so let him take from his friend, from other than what he had given in charity to him’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who gives a certain amount of charity to his friend; if he can change his mind and take it back from him.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so but if he needs he can take from other assets of his friend which is other than what he had given as charity to him.’”
